milestones.title: City of Ji founded
milestones.detail: After the Zhou conquest of the Shang, King Wu enfeoffed a vassal state at Ji, in today's south-west Beijing near Guang'anmen. The city later became the capital of the state of Yan.

milestones.title: Liao dynasty makes the city its Southern Capital
milestones.detail: The Liao renamed Youzhou 'Nanjing' and made it one of their secondary capitals.

milestones.title: Jin capital Zhongdu
milestones.detail: Emperor Wanyan Liang moved the Jin capital here and renamed the city Zhongdu, its first time as the capital of a major dynasty.

milestones.title: Mongols take and burn Zhongdu
milestones.detail: After a long siege the city surrendered to Genghis Khan's army and was looted and burned.
milestones.source: Ratchnevsky (1993), Genghis Khan: His Life and Legacy, pp. 114-115, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Beijing

milestones.title: Kublai Khan begins building Dadu
milestones.detail: Construction of a new capital, Dadu (Khanbaliq), began in 1267; the palace complex was complete by 1274 and the rest of the city by 1285.

milestones.title: Ming army captures Dadu
milestones.detail: General Xu Da took the Yuan capital, which was renamed Beiping; the palace was razed and the northern part of the city abandoned.

milestones.title: Forbidden City completed; capital moves north
milestones.detail: The Yongle Emperor's palace was built from 1406 to 1420, and in 1421 the Ming capital moved from Nanjing to Beijing.

milestones.title: Outer City wall built
milestones.detail: A wall with seven gates was added to protect the southern suburbs, including the Temple of Heaven.

milestones.title: Fall of the Ming; Qing capital
milestones.detail: The Manchus seized Beijing in May 1644 and made it the Qing capital.

milestones.title: Anglo-French forces occupy the city
milestones.detail: In the Second Opium War the allied expedition captured Beijing, and Lord Elgin ordered the Old Summer Palace burned.

milestones.title: Boxer siege of the Legation Quarter
milestones.detail: Qing troops and Boxers besieged the foreign legations from June 1900.

milestones.title: Capital moves to Nanjing; city renamed Beiping
milestones.detail: After the Northern Expedition the Nationalists moved the capital to Nanjing and renamed Beijing 'Beiping'.

milestones.title: Japanese occupation
milestones.detail: After the Marco Polo Bridge clash of 7 July 1937 Japanese forces captured Beiping, which they held until 1945.

milestones.title: Capital of the People's Republic
milestones.detail: The city passed peacefully to Communist control in 1949, was renamed Beijing and became the national capital.

milestones.title: First subway line; city walls pulled down
milestones.detail: The Beijing Subway's first line began trial operations in 1969. Nearly all of the Ming walls were demolished in the 1960s to build it and the 2nd Ring Road.

milestones.title: Summer Olympics
milestones.detail: The 2008 Summer Olympics opened on 8 August at the National Stadium (the 'Bird's Nest').

notes: Start date: 1045 BC is the date the Beijing Municipal Government uses for the founding of Ji (Jicheng), following the Liji account of King Wu of Zhou enfeoffing Ji after conquering the Shang. It rests on later texts, not on a dated foundation, so it is marked 'estimated'; archaeological remains on the Ji site (south and west of Guang'anmen, Xicheng/Fengtai) are dated only from the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods (roughly 8th-5th century BC onward). Historic core: Ji, Tang Youzhou, Liao Nanjing and Jin Zhongdu stood around Guang'anmen (about 39.890 N, 116.344 E), some 5 km south-west of the Forbidden City. Kublai's Dadu (1267) moved the centre to the present axis, and the Ming-Qing walled city grew from there, so the Forbidden City is used as the core for the footprint reconstruction. Population: no city figure was found before 938; Han-to-Tang figures in the sources are for whole commanderies and were not used. The series is Han Guanghui (1996) as quoted in Wikipedia's History of Beijing, and counts people inside the walls only. Two Chandler (1987) points (1500, 1600) fill the 1448-1644 gap but belong to a lower series (Chandler gives 600,000 for 1450 where Han gives 960,000 for 1448; for the 19th century Chandler is higher, 1,648,000 in 1850). Values for 1935 and 1948 are rounded in the source. Landmarks: skyscrapers are from the CTBUH Skyscraper Center; older structures take heights from Wikipedia articles (English or Chinese) and positions from OpenStreetMap. Several old structures are rebuilds, as noted on each. Left out for lack of a sourced height: Bell Tower (sources disagree), Meridian Gate, Deshengmen arrow tower, Olympic Tower.
